step0_family.evidence: The source's structure is one deep egress chain whose content is identifiers and qualifiers: 103.19.91.57/.58/.59/.60-.62, 14.143.x, 14.141.x, 1.1.1.1, AS132717, AS13335, eno16595np0, R7725, plus qualified facts ('free?', 'L2?', 'no cable'). Density is low (9 relations over 9 named elements) and depth is 4 observed hops, so depth alone cannot decide; per tie-breaker 3, identifier and qualifier content outranks shape, which makes this an identity-probe-map. Recipe applied: every identifier and qualifier became a ledger row and got a named view before any spec existed; the layout is the deep chain the recipe calls for, split along the fact clusters the source gives (host NICs, the /29, the DC boundary, the external hops). No spine/leaf nodes were invented.

levers.groups: three single-rank regions. Deliberately single-rank: a region whose members sit in two ranks loses member containment in this engine (measured in attempt 1 and in evidence/hue-probe), because every rank is centred on the widest rank while region bands are column-disjoint. The gateway is therefore left ungrouped here and grouped as 'DC edge' in v3.
levers.layers: none. The source states no geometry; the member->gateway direction is carried by edge direction, and the engine puts the gateway one rank below its members (measured: v2-text.txt rows 34-37).
levers.minlen: none. All three relations are one hop in the source.
levers.trunks: none, deliberately. A trunk is one bus that splits from a single source into branches; the source's /29 relations all run member -> gateway (many -> one), so a trunk would have to reverse the source direction. Plain edges were used instead and the gateway shows three separate arrowheads (v2-text.txt row 33: '▼ ▼ ▼').
